The texts of EnigmaCast. Receiver data such as channel and programme names stay as the receiver sends them.

Own tuner: this device picks its own channel, independent of the receiver. Several devices can watch at the same time, one per free tuner. The receiver may stay in standby; the app draws the channel banner and channel list itself.
Follow receiver: the app switches the receiver to the chosen channel and shows what the receiver shows, with the receiver\'s menu. The remote control operates the receiver.
Fast: less delay, more chance of stutter.
HDMI passes AC3 and E-AC3 through unchanged if the TV supports it.

Is the sound behind the picture? Raise the value until lips and voice match.
How see-through the channel banner, channel list and the receiver OSD are. 0% is solid, 100% is fully clear.
PNG is sharper, JPG is faster on a slow connection.

For %1$s (%2$s), saved with this receiver. Leave the remote profile empty and the tunnel off if you only watch at home.
Off: EnigmaCast starts no VPN and changes no routes; every connection goes straight over the network.
Paste the WireGuard config ([Interface] and [Peer]) in the field below, or import a .conf file. Keys are shown as dots.
This address is on the internet and the connection is plain HTTP: your password and pictures can be read on the way. Use HTTPS, or the remote profile with the WireGuard tunnel.
To watch away from home: the receiver\'s DynDNS name or public address and the ports your router forwards to it. Leave empty if you only watch at home.
Remote host (DynDNS name or public address)
Remote web port (empty: same as home)
Remote stream port (empty: same as home)
HTTPS on the remote web port
Without HTTPS your receiver password goes over the internet readable with every request. Turn on HTTPS in OpenWebif and forward its HTTPS port, or use the WireGuard tunnel.
Enigma2 streams (ports 8001/8002) are always plain HTTP. Over the internet only the WireGuard tunnel encrypts them.
Automatic uses the home address when it answers, and the tunnel or the remote profile otherwise. It checks again when the network changes.
Enter a valid remote host name or address.
Remote ports must be empty or between 1 and 65535.
The transcoding port must be between 1 and 65535.
The stream is not encrypted on the internet.
Stream and password are not encrypted on the internet.
Connected over the internet without encryption. See Stream info.
The original broadcast on the stream port (8001). Best picture; needs the full bitrate, often 5–15 Mbit/s for HD.
The receiver\'s hardware encoder makes a smaller H.264 stream at the size below, at home too. If it does not start, EnigmaCast switches to Normal once and says so.
Normal at home. Over the remote profile or the tunnel transcoded when the receiver reports transcoding; stalls lower the quality, a long stable stretch raises it again.
Automatic starts at 576p away from home and never goes above 720p.

Receivers with a Broadcom encoder use the TranscodingSetup plugin\'s port (usually 8002); other receivers with an encoder transcode on the normal stream port 8001. \"Ask the receiver\" reads it from OpenWebif.
The receiver transcodes on port %1$d; saved.
The receiver offers no transcoding (no hardware encoder, or the TranscodingSetup plugin is missing). Transcoded will switch to Normal.
Could not ask the receiver; enter the port yourself.
Applies from the next channel start. The Quality tile in the player switches at once.
Transcoded stream unavailable; check the TranscodingSetup plugin and port. Switched to normal.
transcoded stream failed, switched to Normal
Normal at home. Over the remote profile or the tunnel a transcoded stream, when the receiver reports transcoding. Stalls lower the quality, a long stable stretch raises it again.
Always the original broadcast (port 8001). Best picture, needs the full bitrate (often 5–15 Mbit/s for HD).
Always the receiver\'s encoder at the chosen size, at home too. Needs a receiver with a hardware encoder; if the transcoded stream fails, EnigmaCast switches to Normal once and says so.

Receivers with a Broadcom encoder transcode on the TranscodingSetup plugin\'s port (8002 or 8001); other receivers with an encoder on the normal stream port 8001. Settings › Playback › Stream type can ask the receiver.

EnigmaCast can start its own WireGuard tunnel to your home network when the receiver does not answer on the home address. The tunnel only carries EnigmaCast\'s traffic and encrypts the streams too. Experimental: it has not been tried on every TV. The official WireGuard app is the more robust choice; with that app running, leave this off and use the home address.
A tunnel config is saved (hidden). Paste or import a new one to replace it.
